items.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: And I’ve been over since then too with a lot of the same guys, Kenny Davern and Yank Lawson and George Masso, and Ralph Sutton, and Jake Hanna.

ctx.x: Yeah, it makes plenty of sense. Tell us about some of your time in Europe with what was called The World’s Greatest Jazz Band.

Milton. We did quite a few trips with the World’s Greatest Jazz Band. And I’ve been over since then too with a lot of the same guys, Kenny Davern and Yank Lawson and George Masso, and Ralph Sutton, and Jake Hanna. But we’ve been over every times it seems it’s a slightly different group. You hardly ever go over with exactly the same personnel. It’s little changes here and there for one reason or another. But the Germans

really seem to love jazz. They won’t let you off the stage, you’ve got to play two encores anyway at the end of a set, and sometimes three, and they get their feet stomping. Clap- stomp at the same time, and that means get ready to play another one. But you’ve got to pretend. You walk off the stage and you wait out there and then say, “Guess we’re going to do another one,” and start ambling back on again. You play a second one, and it starts over again. They don’t do that over here. I mean there’s something about…
